requests.reason: Inspect FileSnapshotStore construction, Create, List, Open and retention helpers preceding the acquired Close implementation. Establish how to obtain a real sink, induce a publication failure after successful writes, and independently observe whether its ID is available. Distinguish an unpublished snapshot from a published snapshot whose later synchronization or reaping failed.

audit_question.question: When takeSnapshot consumes a successful FileSnapshotSink.Close result, do the applicable sink and FSMSnapshot.Persist contracts ensure that the snapshot has completed the publication steps needed before snapshot metadata advances and logs are compacted, including legally reachable repeated-close and prior-error paths?
audit_question.importance: Accepting incomplete publication before reclaiming logs could remove recovery evidence. The immediate discriminator is completion-result interpretation; actual recovery loss requires a separate legal history and recovery analysis.
contexts: Repository middleware-testing snapshot implementation; deployment applicability unresolved
event_paths: FSM snapshot capture -> FSMSnapshot.Persist -> sink Close -> last-snapshot update -> log compaction
MockSnapshot.Persist encoding succeeds -> initial sink.Close result discarded -> Persist returns nil -> takeSnapshot calls Close again
counterevidence: FSMSnapshot.Persist and SnapshotSink document completion by Close and cancellation on error; they do not explicitly define repeated Close results following a failed completion.
takeSnapshot checks Persist and its subsequent Close before advancing metadata or compacting logs. Propagating the initial Close error through Persist prevents the suspected continuation.
A fresh FileSnapshotSink.Close checks finalization, metadata writing, rename, applicable directory synchronization and reaping. writeMeta checks encoding, flushing and conditional synchronization.
Some Close failures occur after rename; a Close error alone does not establish that the snapshot is unavailable.

TestFileSS_CreateSnapshot asserts listing and readable matching contents after a successful fresh Close. TestFileSS_CancelSnapshot asserts absence after cancellation. These assertions do not cover failed Close followed by repeated Close.
MockSnapshot is explicitly exposed for middleware testing and is not a stable API. Its error handling does not establish the contract or behavior of arbitrary application snapshots.
Compaction retains the configured trailing range and never deletes beyond the snapshot index. A completion mismatch alone does not establish recovery loss.
unknowns: Whether the applicable contract requires Persist to propagate every sink completion error; the attached comments do not state this explicitly.
Whether repeated Close after a failed Close has an independently supported success meaning, rather than merely being a tolerated repeated resource operation.
Whether a contract-compliant Persist can return nil after incomplete publication, including a prior failed Close or cancellation.
How broadly the fresh-success publication expectations in file_snapshot_test.go apply to repeated completion after failure.
Which application Persist implementation and snapshot adapter are selected in an actual deployment.
Which publication guarantees apply under noSync and operating-system variants; conditional synchronization is visible, but crash durability is not established.
Whether any locally distinguishable completion mismatch can cause loss of recovery evidence in a legal history.
Which controlled failure can occur after MockSnapshot encoding succeeds but before file snapshot publication, using the actual constructor and sink resources.
How List, Open and retention distinguish failed publication, successful publication with a later error, and subsequent removal.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The acquired MockSnapshot.Persist implementation concretely discards sink.Close errors and returns nil after successful encoding. Combined with FileSnapshotSink.Close setting closed before fallible publication and returning nil on subsequent calls, this identifies an actual repository callback path for the suspected interpretation mismatch. It does not establish callback contract compliance, deployment selection or recovery loss. The next read establishes the real adapter setup and independent publication oracle needed to decide whether a bounded local obligation is justified.

selection_rationale: Continue the same Fact consumption question. The new source resolves whether a repository callback can discard the first completion error: MockSnapshot.Persist does so. The complete file snapshot test file supplies fresh-success publication assertions but no failed-then-repeated Close expectation. Existing check IDs have no supplied execution results or evidence IDs, so neither reproduction nor protection is established. Before deriving a local obligation or a linked child, inspect the concrete Create/List/Open boundary: observing an unavailable ID after apparent completion would discriminate publication from resource closure, while observing an available ID after a post-publication error would require a narrower interpretation. This read serves the existing endpoint and does not require proving broader recovery loss.
